title: Split chip data from a log into its objects

blocks.text: A network has started declining some chip transactions, and the support desk is reading DE 55 from hex dumps in the logs. They want a small tool that prints each object in the dump, and that says so when a dump is damaged instead of printing a guess, because a guess is what they would act on.
`TlvReader` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/TlvReader.java` already walks the data and collects the objects. Finish the three methods marked `TODO`:

items: `tagEnd`: where the tag that starts at a position ends;
`lengthAt`: the value's length, and where the value starts;

blocks.text: Dumps come from several card schemes, so expect tags and lengths beyond the common ones. Refuse what can't be split with an `IllegalArgumentException`; `byteAt` already refuses to read past the end. About 15 lines in total.

cases.says: the chip data of an ordinary authorization comes out as its objects, in order, each with its own value
a first byte with its low five bits all ones starts a longer tag, whatever the byte, not only 9F
a tag goes on while each further byte has its top bit set, so tags are not limited to two bytes
a length of 128 or more is written as 81 or 82 followed by the length, and the value is read whole
a value that claims more bytes than remain is refused, never filled up

origin.section: 3.6. DE 55 Is a List of Tag-Length-Value Objects, Read as Bytes

concepts: DE 55 is a list of BER-TLV objects: a tag that continues while its bytes say so, a length in one byte or after 81 or 82, and exactly that many value bytes.
